retrieved.title: About This Handbook and Northbridge Institute
retrieved.text: This handbook sets out the official student policies of Northbridge Institute of Management & Technology (a fictional institution) for the academic year 2026–27. It applies to all students enrolled in the MBA, PGDM, BBA, B.Tech CSE and M.Tech Data Science programmes. The academic year is divided into three terms: Term 1 (July to October), Term 2 (November to February) and Term 3 (March to June). All amounts in this handbook are in Indian Rupees (INR). Where this handbook and a programme-specific notice differ, the more recent notice issued by the Registrar's Office applies. Students are expected to read this handbook at the start of each academic year and to check the student portal regularly for updates. Questions about any policy can be raised through the support ticket system described in the section on raising a support request.

retrieved.title: Programme Transfer
retrieved.text: Students may apply to transfer from one programme to another only at the end of an academic year. Transfers are allowed only between programmes at the same level (undergraduate to undergraduate, postgraduate to postgraduate) with compatible entry requirements; for example, a transfer from PGDM to MBA may be considered, but a transfer from BBA to B.Tech CSE is not permitted. The application must be submitted to the Registrar's Office by 31 May, with a statement of purpose and the consent of the current Programme Director. The receiving programme's admissions committee decides whether credits already earned will be recognised. A student may transfer programmes only once during their studies. If approved, the fee for the new programme applies from the following term, and any scholarship is reassessed under the new programme's rules. Mid-year transfers are not permitted.

question: The online payment portal isn't working and today is the fee due date. What should I do?
answer:
**Here’s what to do when the fee‑payment portal is down on the due date** (Policy [chunk‑05] – *Payment Portal Failures on the Due Date*):

1. **Try again briefly** – sometimes the portal comes back online within a few minutes.  
2. **Capture the error** – take a screenshot (or note the exact error message) and record the date & time of the failed attempt.  
3. **Report the outage within 24 hours** – you have two options:  
   - **Raise a Finance‑category support ticket** (you can let me create it for you).  
   - **Email finance@northbridge.edu** with the screenshot/error, date, and time.  
4. **Pay on the next working day** – after reporting, you can settle the fee on the following business day without any late‑payment charge.  
5. **Keep the confirmation** – once the payment is successful, verify that the payment reflects in your student portal.

Would you like me to raise a Finance support ticket for you now? (I’ll include the details you’ve provided.)

retrieved.title: Payment Portal Failures on the Due Date
retrieved.text: If the online fee payment portal fails or is unavailable on the due date, the student will not be penalised for the outage. In this case the student may pay on the next working day without any late fee, provided that the student reports the failure within 24 hours of the failed attempt. The report must be made either by raising a support ticket in the Finance category or by emailing finance@northbridge.edu, and it must include a screenshot or the exact error message shown, together with the date and time of the attempt. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays notified by the Institute. For example, if the due date falls on a Friday and the portal fails, payment must be completed by the following Monday (or Tuesday if Monday is a public holiday). If the failure is not reported within 24 hours, normal late payment fees apply.

retrieved.title: Late Payment Fees and Registration Block
retrieved.text: Fees not received by the due date attract a late payment fee of ₹500 per calendar day, starting the day after the due date. The total late fee for any one term is capped at ₹7,500. The late fee is added to the student's outstanding balance and appears on the fee statement in the student portal. If fees remain unpaid more than 15 days after the due date, the student's registration for the term is blocked. A blocked student cannot add or drop courses, access the learning management system, or receive hall tickets for examinations until all dues, including late fees, are cleared. The block is lifted automatically within one working day of full payment. Late fees may be waived only in the case of a reported portal failure (see the section on payment portal failures) or with written approval from the Finance Controller for documented emergencies.

retrieved.title: Accepted Payment Methods
retrieved.text: Fees can be paid through the official online fee payment portal using net banking, UPI, or debit and credit cards issued by Indian banks. Card payments may attract a convenience charge levied by the payment gateway, which is shown before the payment is confirmed. Fees can also be paid by NEFT or RTGS transfer to the Institute's bank account; the account details are printed on the fee statement, and the student ID must be entered in the transfer remarks. Demand drafts in favour of "Northbridge Institute of Management & Technology" are accepted at the Finance Office counter during office hours. Cash payments are not accepted for fees above ₹10,000. Education loan disbursements paid directly by a bank to the Institute are accepted, but the student remains responsible for ensuring the amount reaches the Institute by the due date.

retrieved.title: Instalment Plans
retrieved.text: Students who cannot pay the full term fee at once may apply for an instalment plan. Under the standard plan, the term fee is split into two instalments: 60% due on the regular due date and 40% due 45 days later. Applications must be submitted through the student portal under Finance > Instalment Request at least 7 days before the term due date, and must include a short statement of reasons. If an instalment is missed, the plan is cancelled and the full remaining balance becomes due immediately, with late fees calculated from the original instalment date. Only one instalment plan may be approved per academic year.

question: The add/drop deadline has passed. Can I still change my elective?
answer:
You can still change an elective, but only under **exceptional circumstances** (e.g., a timetable clash, a medical reason, or a course cancelled by the Institute).

**What you need to do**

- **Submit the Course Change Form CC‑2**  
  - Find it in the portal under **Academics > Forms**.  
  - Attach a brief written justification for the change.
- **Get approval**  
  - The request must be approved by your Programme Director (they may consult the relevant faculty).
- **Pay the processing fee**  
  - ₹1,000 for each approved late change (waived only if the Institute cancelled the course).
- **Timing**  
  - Requests are normally decided within **5 working days**.  
  - Late changes are **not allowed after week 6 of the term**.

If you meet one of the exceptional criteria, go ahead and submit the form. Otherwise, the change won’t be possible after the add/drop window. Let me know if you’d like help locating the form or need any other assistance!

The request requires approval from the Programme Director, who may consult the faculty teaching both courses. A non-refundable processing fee of ₹1,000 applies to every approved late course change; the fee is waived if the change is caused by the Institute cancelling a course. retrieved.title: Course Add/Drop Window
retrieved.text: Students may add or drop courses during the add/drop window, which is the first two weeks (14 calendar days) of each term. All changes are made online through the student portal under Academics > Course Registration. Adding a course is subject to seat availability and to any prerequisites listed in the course catalogue. Dropping a course within the window does not appear on the transcript and has no fee consequence. Students must keep the minimum credit load for their programme after any drop; the portal will not allow a change that takes a student below the minimum. Changes take effect immediately, and the student's timetable is updated within one working day. Students are advised to attend the first sessions of a course before deciding. Students with a registration block due to unpaid fees cannot use the add/drop function until the block is lifted.

retrieved.title: Raising a Support Request
retrieved.text: Students can raise a support request (ticket) through the student portal under Help > New Ticket, or by asking the AI Student Support Agent to create one. Each ticket must have a category: Finance (fees, payments, receipts, refunds), Academics (courses, exams, attendance), Scholarships, IT (Wi-Fi, email, portal login, software), Hostel and Facilities, or General. Students can track ticket status on the portal.

retrieved.title: Fee Structure and Fee Components
retrieved.text: Each term's fee is made up of several components, all shown separately on the fee statement in the student portal. The tuition fee covers teaching, course materials and access to the learning management system. The academic services fee covers examinations, library access, laboratory use and career services. The technology fee covers campus Wi-Fi, software licences and the student email account. A one-time caution deposit of ₹10,000 is collected in Term 1 of the first year and is refundable on graduation or withdrawal after deducting any dues. Indicative term fees for 2026–27 are: MBA and PGDM ₹1,85,000; M.Tech Data Science ₹1,40,000; B.Tech CSE ₹1,10,000; BBA ₹75,000. The total payable for a term is the sum of all components minus any approved scholarship adjustment. Optional charges, such as elective study tours, are billed separately and are not part of the term fee.

retrieved.title: Scholarship Disbursement
retrieved.text: Approved Institute scholarships are not paid to students in cash. Instead, the scholarship amount is adjusted against the student's fees, normally split equally across the remaining terms of the academic year. The adjustment appears as a credit line on the fee statement, and the student pays only the balance. If a scholarship is approved after the student has already paid the full term fee, the credit is carried forward to the next term; any excess at the end of the academic year is refunded to the student's verified bank account. External scholarships paid to the Institute by a third party are credited in the same way once the funds are received. While a scholarship is under review, the student must pay fees as normal by the due date; the scholarship credit will be applied once approved. Scholarships are withdrawn if the student withdraws from the programme.

retrieved.title: Scholarship Eligibility and Renewal Criteria
retrieved.text: To be eligible for any Institute scholarship, a student must be enrolled full-time, have no disciplinary action recorded in the current year, and have no overdue fees at the time of application. Merit Scholarship renewal requires a minimum CGPA of 7.5 at the end of the previous academic year and at least 75% attendance in every course. Need-Based Scholarship renewal requires updated income documents each year and a minimum CGPA of 6.0. Sports Scholarship renewal requires a minimum CGPA of 6.0 and a satisfactory participation report from the Sports Committee. A student whose CGPA falls below the required level loses the scholarship for the following year but may reapply once the criteria are met again. Students found to have submitted false information will have the scholarship cancelled and must repay any amounts already adjusted.

retrieved.title: Scholarship Disbursement
retrieved.text: Approved Institute scholarships are not paid to students in cash. Instead, the scholarship amount is adjusted against the student's fees, normally split equally across the remaining terms of the academic year. The adjustment appears as a credit line on the fee statement, and the student pays only the balance. If a scholarship is approved after the student has already paid the full term fee, the credit is carried forward to the next term; any excess at the end of the academic year is refunded to the student's verified bank account. External scholarships paid to the Institute by a third party are credited in the same way once the funds are received. While a scholarship is under review, the student must pay fees as normal by the due date; the scholarship credit will be applied once approved. Scholarships are withdrawn if the student withdraws from the programme.

retrieved.title: Scholarship Application Process and Deadlines
retrieved.text: Scholarship applications are submitted online through the student portal under Scholarships > Apply. Applicants must upload the relevant documents: mark sheets for merit applications, family income certificates and the latest income tax return for need-based applications, and sports certificates for sports applications. For 2026–27, the application window for continuing students runs from 1 August to 15 September 2026; first-year students apply at the time of admission. The Scholarship Committee reviews applications in two rounds, and results are published on the portal by 31 October for the first round and by 30 November for the second round. While an application is being assessed, its status is shown as "under review". Incomplete applications are not considered. Students may appeal a rejection within 10 working days of the decision by writing to scholarships@northbridge.edu.

retrieved.title: Raising a Support Request
retrieved.text: Students can raise a support request (ticket) through the student portal under Help > New Ticket, or by asking the AI Student Support Agent to create one. Each ticket must have a category: Finance (fees, payments, receipts, refunds), Academics (courses, exams, attendance), Scholarships, IT (Wi-Fi, email, portal login, software), Hostel and Facilities, or General. Every ticket receives a reference number in the format TKT-XXXX, which the student should quote in any follow-up. Target first-response times are: Finance and Scholarships within 2 working days; Academics within 2 working days; IT within 1 working day; Hostel and Facilities within 1 working day; General within 3 working days. Tickets marked Urgent, for example a portal failure on a fee due date or an issue preventing exam access, receive a first response within 4 hours during office hours. Students can track ticket status on the portal.

retrieved.title: Fee Receipts and Statements
retrieved.text: A digital fee receipt is generated automatically for every successful payment and can be downloaded from the student portal under Finance > Receipts. Receipts for online payments are normally available within 2 hours; receipts for NEFT, RTGS and demand draft payments are issued within 3 working days of the funds being credited. Each receipt shows the student ID, term, amount, payment method, transaction reference and date. The consolidated fee statement for the academic year, often required by banks for education loans or by employers for reimbursement, can also be downloaded from the portal. If a payment has been debited from the student's account but no receipt appears after 3 working days, the student should raise a Finance support ticket with the transaction reference. Duplicate stamped receipts can be requested from the Finance Office at no charge.

retrieved.title: Contact Details and Office Hours
retrieved.text: The main student-facing offices are open Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 5:30 pm, excluding public holidays, and on the first Saturday of each month from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm. The Finance Office (fees, payments and refunds) can be reached at finance@northbridge.edu or extension 2210. The Scholarships Cell is at scholarships@northbridge.edu, extension 2240. The Registrar's Office (registration, transfers, withdrawal and records) is at registrar@northbridge.edu, extension 2100. The IT Help Desk is at ithelp@northbridge.edu, extension 2300, and also operates a phone line from 8:00 am to 10:00 pm on weekdays. Academic queries should first go to the student's Programme Office. For anything not covered here, students should raise a General support ticket, and the request will be routed to the right team.

retrieved.title: Student Data Privacy and Security
retrieved.text: The Institute processes student data in line with applicable Indian data protection law and uses it only for academic, administrative and support purposes. Students can only view their own records; staff and support systems will not disclose one student's fee, scholarship, grade or personal information to another student. Institute staff, including the AI Student Support Agent, will never ask for a student's password, OTP (one-time password), full card number, CVV or UPI PIN. Students must not share these details in emails, chats or support tickets; if they are shared by mistake, they will not be stored, and the student should change the password or contact their bank immediately. Sensitive information such as health details is recorded only when needed for an approved process, such as academic leave. Students may request a copy of their personal data from the Data Protection Officer at privacy@northbridge.edu.
